project_summary.name: Forge-AI
project_summary.description: Natural language to production-ready full-stack application using a coordinated multi-agent AI pipeline. Users describe an app idea and the system generates all files (React + Vite + FastAPI + MongoDB) with real-time streaming, deployment, and billing.
project_summary.competitive_landscape: Direct competitor to Emergent.sh, Bolt.new (StackBlitz), v0.dev (Vercel), and Lovable. Differentiator: 6-agent pipeline with business model validation and PM QA agent.
project_summary.target_audience: Solo developers, startup founders, and indie hackers who want to rapidly prototype and ship full-stack applications
project_summary.confidence: High — comprehensive code audit completed across 70+ files covering all backend modules, frontend components, API endpoints, database models, and infrastructure configuration.

frontend.realtime: Native WebSocket API with exponential backoff reconnection hook

backend.auth: JWT via python-jose[cryptography] 3.3 + bcrypt via passlib 1.7
backend.billing: Stripe SDK 8.9 with webhook signature verification

infrastructure.containers: Docker Compose with 4 services (backend, frontend, mongo, redis)
infrastructure.storage: MongoDB 7 with authentication via docker-compose env vars
infrastructure.network: Single Docker bridge network, localhost-exposed ports
missing_critical: Monitoring and alerting (no Prometheus / OpenTelemetry / Sentry)
Structured logging / log aggregation (no ELK / Loki / Datadog)
Secrets management (no HashiCorp Vault / AWS Secrets Manager)
Migration strategy for database schema changes

architecture.pattern: Multi-agent AI pipeline orchestrator with real-time WebSocket event streaming to SPA frontend
architecture.pipeline_flow: User describes app in natural language → POST /builds creates Build → BackgroundTask starts Orchestrator → [Architect → BusinessModelImprover → Designer → Developer (streaming) → Integration → Sandbox → PM QA] → WebSocket events → Zustand store → React UI updates
architecture.agent_contract: Each agent receives structured JSON from upstream, calls Anthropic Claude API with role-specific system prompt, outputs structured JSON. Architect produces blueprint JSON, Developer produces file dict {path: content}, PM produces validation report with score.
architecture.realtime_protocol: WebSocket connections authenticated via JWT in URL query param (SECURITY ISSUE). Event types: agent_start, agent_progress, agent_complete, file_update, build_complete, build_failed, debug_start, stream_token, credits_update.

state_management.build_state: In-memory Build Pydantic object mutated directly (no state machine / event sourcing)
state_management.persistence: MongoDB full document write after every agent step (high write amplification at scale)
state_management.webSocket_connections: Python dict[build_id] → List[WebSocket] in ws_manager.py (lost on restart, cannot scale horizontally)

key_architectural_issues: Orchestrator runs in FastAPI BackgroundTasks (blocks all workers during long builds)
Celery dependency installed but never wired — builds execute in-process
WebSocket connection registry is in-memory only (zero availability during deploys)
Build state mutated via direct attribute assignment (no state machine pattern)
No circuit breaker or exponential backoff for Anthropic API calls
No build timeout or cancellation mechanism (background task runs indefinitely)
Full file dict (potentially MBs) transmitted on every WebSocket event instead of deltas
No event sourcing — partial build state lost if orchestrator fails mid-pipeline
Single MongoDB document stores all build files (hits 16MB BSON limit for complex apps)
scalability_blockers: Single-process bottleneck (BackgroundTasks cannot distribute across workers)
In-memory WebSocket registry prevents multi-worker or multi-instance deployment
MongoDB-based rate limiting adds 2-5ms overhead per request (should be Redis O(1))
Unbounded to_list(None) on admin and builds queries (OOM risk at scale)
Zero HTTP response caching on any endpoint
get_current_user hits MongoDB on every authenticated request (should use Redis cache)
security_weaknesses: Docker socket mounted in web-facing container (full host compromise possible)
No CSRF protection (all POST endpoints vulnerable with cookie auth)
JWT secret defaults to empty string if .env not configured
WebSocket JWT token transmitted in URL query parameter (logged, leaked in Referer)
No prompt injection defense (user input directly injected into AI system prompts)
GitHub tokens embedded in git clone URLs (visible in ps aux, stored in .git/config)
Rate limiting IP spoofable via X-Forwarded-For header
MongoDB and Redis had no authentication in earlier config (fixed in docker-compose)
No input length validation on critical fields (prompt field unbounded)

overall_risk: CRITICAL — The system has 17 P0 security vulnerabilities (including Docker socket container escape enabling full host compromise), zero automated test coverage, and fundamental architecture blockers that prevent production deployment. Credit race conditions enable unlimited revenue leakage. The orchestrator runs in-process blocking all workers, so the application becomes completely unavailable during builds. No build timeout or cancellation exists — a stuck build consumes resources forever. WebSocket state is ephemeral in-memory only, causing zero availability during deploys. The 16MB MongoDB BSON document limit will be hit for any moderately complex app build. Estimated 212 person-hours to reach production-ready baseline. Risk tolerance: ZERO — do not deploy publicly before Phase 1 and Phase 2 completion.
estimated_review_time: Audit complete. Implementation estimate: ~212 person-hours across 8 specialized agents over 5 ordered phases. Phase 1 (Security + DevOps, 48h) and Phase 2 (Architecture + Database, 60h) are gating and must be completed before any production deployment. Phases 3 (Product + Frontend, 48h) and 4 (Testing, 40h) can run in parallel after Phases 1-2. Phase 5 (Performance, 16h) is post-stabilization optimization.
